turns.t: Mr Venkataraman, the booking says you want a review and that something to do with an old reaction is worrying you.
Yes, yes, doctor. Please call me Venkat, everyone does. That reaction business I will come to, but first let me tell you about this chest.
Go ahead. What is the chest doing?
When I climb the stairs to my daughter's flat, third floor only, I get a tightness here in the middle. Then I stop, wait, and it goes.
So tightness in the middle of the chest when you climb. How long has this been happening?
For about one month only. Before that I was climbing like a goat. My grandson says I am slowing down.
How long does it last when you stop?
Two minutes, maybe three. I have to hold the railing and pretend I am admiring the view.
Ha. Does it spread anywhere, the arm or the jaw?
Not that I noticed. Same spot every time.
Have you been short of breath with it?
No, no. Breath is fine. Only the tightness, and my heart doesn't flutter or anything like that.
Good. Now, tell me about the reaction. What's worrying you?
See, my cousin in Chennai had a terrible thing with a tablet. He nearly died, doctor. So now I am worried about every tablet.
I'm sorry to hear that. But I'm asking about you. Do you have a reaction of your own?
Yes. Years ago, I took some antibiotic for my throat and I reacted to it. My wife was there, she remembers more than me.
What kind of reaction? A rash, swelling, breathing trouble?
That is the problem, I cannot recall. I only remember the doctor said, never take that antibiotic again. Hospital people made a note.
Do you remember the name?
No. It was something ending in 'cillin' or maybe 'mycin'. I told my wife to remember but she says ask Venkat.
Ha. So we know it's an antibiotic, and you had some kind of reaction, but not which one or what happened.
Exactly. Is it a problem? Because you will be giving me tablets also, no?
I'm not prescribing anything today. But I want it on your record as an allergy to an antibiotic, so nobody gives you the wrong one.
Good. Good. That is why I came. My wife was telling me, do it before the next emergency.
Sensible wife. Can you find the old hospital papers? Or ask your wife whether she kept the discharge letter?
She keeps everything. Forty-five years of marriage and she has every bill. I will search the almirah.
Please bring whatever you find. Also, if the old GP's surgery still exists, we can ask them for the note.
That one is closed now. The doctor retired, and his son went to Dubai.
Then the papers at home are our best chance. What did you do for work, Venkat?
I am a retired bank manager. Thirty-five years in the State Bank. Many files, I know the value of a record.
Then you'll appreciate this. A clear record is worth more than ten guesses.
Let me repeat that back to be sure. Tightness on the stairs for a month, settling in minutes, and an antibiotic reaction years ago, details unknown.
Correct. You should work for the bank, doctor. Tell me one thing. This chest tightness. Is it dangerous?
I can't say yet, and I don't want to guess. That is exactly why I'd like to see you again once the papers are found.
Okay. When should I come?
Let's say in four weeks. That gives you time to search the almirah and ask around.
Four weeks is fine. Should my wife come along? She remembers more than me.
Please do bring her. Two memories are better than one.
Good. Four weeks is fine. Should I climb those stairs in the meantime?
Take the lift if there is one, and rest when the tightness comes. If it lasts longer than ten minutes, call an ambulance.
Ten minutes. I will tell my daughter also. She will be so anxious.
Tell her yes. And Venkat, thank you for being so organised about this.
It's my pleasure. Thank you, doctor. I will bring the papers and some of my wife's homemade sweets.
The papers will do nicely. Goodbye, and mind the stairs.

chief_complaint.value: I get a tightness here in the middle

clinical_actions.description: Bring old hospital papers or discharge letter identifying the antibiotic and reaction
Rest when tightness comes; call an ambulance if it lasts longer than ten minutes
